description.narrative:
Saferworld is an independent international organization that works with research, policy development, capacity building and implementation of programs aimed at preventing violence and conflict. Saferworld conducts conflict prevention and peacebuilding work in Africa, the Middle East, Asia and Europe. Currently, Saferworld's geographical focus is on the following countries: Kenya, Somalia / Somaliland, Sudan and South Sudan, Uganda, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Syria and Yemen.
By utilizing local knowledge and building on the experiences of conflict-affected individuals and society, Saferworld works to improve and strengthen local, national and international peacebuilding for long-term sustainable development.
Sida has received an application for core support from Saferworld. The proposal is to support Saferworld's new five-year strategic plan (2021-2025) with a total amount of SEK 90 800 000 over three years (1 April 2021 - 31 March 2024), which corresponds to approximately 13% percent of Saferworld's total budget. Part of the support will be earmarked with an average of SEK 5 million per year for the purpose of working with control and against the spread of small and light weapons, as well as compliance with the Arms Trade Treaty. Sida has contributed core support to Saferworld since 2014 and this will thus be a continuation of this collaboration

Saferworld är en oberoende internationell organisation som arbetar med forskning, policyutveckling, kapacitetsbyggande och genomförande av program med syfte att förhindra våld och konflikt. Saferworld bedriver konfliktförebyggande och fredsbyggande arbete i Afrika, Mellanöstern, Asien och Europa. För närvarande är Saferworlds geografiska fokus följande länder: Kenya, Somalia/ Somaliland, Sudan och Sydsudan, Uganda, Kirgizistan, Tadjikistan, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Nepal, Syrien och Yemen.
Genom att tillvarata lokal kunskap och utgå från konfliktdrabbade individers och samhällets erfarenheter arbetar Saferworld för att förbättra och stärka lokalt, nationellt och internationellt fredsbyggande för långsiktig hållbar utveckling.
Sida har mottagit en ansökan om kärnstöd från Saferworld. Förslaget är att stödja Saferworlds nya femåriga strategiska plan (2021- 2025) med ett totalt belopp om 90 800 000 SEK över tre år (1 april 2021 - 31 mars 2024), vilket motsvarar cirka 13% procent av Saferworlds totala budget. En del av stödet kommer att öronmärkas med i genomsnitt 5 MSEK per år för ändamålet att arbeta med kontroll och mot spridning av små och lätta vapen, samt efterlevnad av Vapenhandelsfördraget. Sida har bidragit med kärnstöd till Saferworld sedan 2014 och detta blir därmed en fortsättning på detta samarbete.

To contribute to prevention of violent conflict and strengthen human security, the core support from Sida will, for the period 2021-2026, contribute to the following five interlinked goals set out in Saferworld's Strategic Plan Working in solidarity for a safer world 2021-2031:
i) Inclusive peace and justice: Communities and CSOs, in particular women and youth, in conflict-affected contexts lead efforts to achieve conflict transformation and political transitions rooted in equality and justice by working with authorities and each other across conflict divides, and with relevant external actors.
ii) People-centred security: External actors, governments, and state and non-state security actors increasingly recognise and move away from harmful militarised and repressive approaches to conflict and security, and towards a people-centred and more accountable understanding of human security.
iii) Gender Equality: Donors, peacebuilding organisations and policymakers, communities, civil society and authorities address gender norms and patriarchal systems and structures driving exclusion, conflict and insecurity, and promote gender equality and womens meaningful participation and leadership through their programming and policies.
iv) Redesigning international engagement: International actors in conflict-affected and fragile settings realign their systems, instruments and resources to underpin peaceful change and transformation from within, putting local leadership in the driving seat.
v) Climate, conflict and the environment: Communities, CSOs, authorities (local, state, national) and international actors recognise the effects of climate change on conflict dynamics; collaboration between peacebuilding and environmental practitioners is strengthened; and strategies to incorporate climate change and conflict prevention are developed around more holistic responses.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
Under the Strategic Objective 1 (Inclusive peace and Justice), Saferworld has reported many achievements under the reporting period, some of which are highlighted below:
Saferworld continued to support communities, civil society organisations and informal groups to strengthen their capacities, agency and leadership in peacebuilding processes across a number of conflict-affected contexts. In Sudan, Saferworld together with its partners provided technical guidance, coaching and monitoring support to community-led initiatives implemented through Mutual Aid Groups. A total of 549 micro-grants were awarded to support activities ranging from food security and livelihoods to protection, health, water and sanitation, shelter and other emergency humanitarian needs. Similar to previous years, Sida views this approach positively as it demonstrates Saferworlds continued commitment to strengthening locally owned responses in highly fragile contexts while maintaining flexibility during ongoing conflict. In Kyrgyzstan, Saferworld supported partners working with youth groups, providing training and knowledge aimed at strengthening young peoples ability to contribute positively to their communities and engage in social initiatives. In Myanmar, support to citizen journalism initiatives helped strengthen the capacity of local communities to document and communicate their realities, amplifying voices that are often absent from mainstream media. Sida assesses that these initiatives demonstrate how peacebuilding efforts can be linked to broader participation and civic engagement processes. Saferworld continued to provide increasingly flexible support to civil society organisations in fragile and conflict-affected settings. Particularly noteworthy was the creation of a network bringing together nine organisations from Sudan, Syria and Yemen, enabling them to exchange experiences, develop joint responses to regional challenges and engage collectively with potential donors. Sida views this as an example of an important and potentially sustainable outcome, as it strengthens horizontal linkages between civil society actors and may contribute to greater resilience and organisational sustainability over time. In Syria, Saferworld supported four civil society organisations to establish a consortium focused on sustainable peacebuilding, womens participation, youth engagement and inclusion of persons with disabilities while seeking to strengthen connections across conflict divides. Given the continued volatility in Syria and the political developments during the reporting period, Sida sees this as a particularly relevant and timely intervention. In Yemen, the Civic Voices Hub continued to strengthen the juvenile justice system through support to the Juvenile Care and Rehabilitation Centre, including vocational training, advocacy initiatives and rehabilitation of facilities. The initiative reportedly strengthened protection mechanisms and improved conditions for juveniles in conflict with the law. Sida assesses this as a good example of how peacebuilding approaches can be connected to justice and service delivery systems at local level. In Somalia, Saferworld continued implementation of its Early Warning, Early Response (EWER) approach through community- and CSO-led centres aimed at identifying and addressing potential conflicts before they escalate. Over 50 government representatives from institutions including police, district administrations and relevant ministries participated. Joint advocacy and communication efforts by local partners contributed to strengthening community engagement and promoting more inclusive conflict prevention mechanisms. In Uganda, Kenya and South Sudan, Saferworld continued to support locally led responses to the interconnected challenges of conflict, climate change and gender inequality in border areas. One example is the establishment of a transboundary trade forum designed to foster peaceful cross-border trade and support dialogue between actors across conflict divides. Sida sees this as an indication of Saferworld increasingly working at the intersection of peacebuilding, climate adaptation and economic resilience.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
